chunks: And my father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ubaydillah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Nahawandi, from Abi Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn Thuwayr, from Yunus and Abi Salamah al-Sarraj and al-Mufaḍḍal ibn 'Umar, who said: We heard Aba 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
When al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) died, all that Allah created wept for him except for three things: Basra, Damascus, and the family of 'Uthman.

key_terms.الْبَصْرَةَ: Basra, a major city in Iraq
key_terms.وَدِمَشْقَ: and Damascus, a major city in Syria

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet's family and creation weep for upon the death of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that upon the death of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him), the entire creation of Allah wept for him, with the exception of three specific entities: the city of Basra, the city of Damascus, and the family of 'Uman. This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic scale of the tragedy, linking the political centers of Umayyad power (Damascus) and their regional stronghold (Basra) to the familial lineage of the usurper 'Uthman, symbolizing the enduring enmity of the ruling elite against the Ahl al-Bayt.
